text:
ConocoPhillips dropped 5.2% today as crude oil prices fell sharply, sliding below $90 a barrel on Wednesday. The decline was triggered by shifting political sentiment around the Iran conflict—Vice President Vance publicly blamed Republican midterm election losses on the ongoing war, and both U.S. and Iranian leadership signaled openness to diplomatic negotiations. Since oil refiners and producers earn more when crude prices are higher, the prospect of de-escalation and lower oil prices directly pressures their valuations.

The stock has now fallen nearly 6% over two weeks as oil market sentiment has turned. Geopolitical risk—the possibility of war disrupting supply—has been a major prop supporting oil prices; when that risk recedes, prices fall with it, and energy stocks follow.
